sections.body: MISINFORMATION is false information shared by mistake. DISINFORMATION is false information spread on purpose.
DEEPFAKES are AI-made videos, images or audio that make it look like someone said or did something they didn't.
Check: Is the source reliable? Do other trusted outlets report it? Does the image look odd (hands, shadows, blurry edges)? Try a reverse image search.
Pause before sharing, especially if it makes you angry or shocked. Emotions spread fakes fastest.

quiz.q: What's the difference between misinformation and disinformation?
hints: One is a mistake, one is deliberate.
Accidentally telling someone the wrong time is a mistake; lying about the time to make them late is deliberate.
quiz.explain: Disinformation is false information spread on purpose. Misinformation is spread by mistake.

quiz.q: You see a shocking video of a politician saying something outrageous. What first?
options: Check if trusted news outlets report it
Assume it's real because it's video
hints: Do other reliable sources confirm it?
Before believing a rumour about a classmate, you'd check with others who were there.
quiz.explain: Check whether trusted outlets confirm it. Videos can be deepfakes.
